newsitem.title: USA: Columbus plans $125 mln private hockey arena.
newsitem.headline: Columbus plans $125 mln private hockey arena.

text.p: Columbus, Ohio, hockey boosters completed a plan to build a $125 million privately financed arena with infrastructure and improvements paid by the city and Franklin County convention center authority, the convention center executive director said Wednesday.
Nationwide Insurance Co would finance 90 percent of the arena and the Dispatch Printing Co 10 percent if the National Hockey League awards Columbus an expansion franchise, William Jennison said.

Columbus City Council voted Monday night to spend just under $20 million to demolish, cleanup and provide infrastructure to the former Ohio Penitentiary site downtown as part of the project, Jennison noted.
Ohio deeded the 22-acre prison to Columbus in summer 1995 and under the plans approved Monday, the city would provide Nationwide with a 10-year lease to use it as surface parking, Jennison said.
Nationwide would then have the option of buying the land for further development, Jennison said.

The convention authority has already agreed to spend $3 million to $5 million of reserves to acquire land adjacent to the city-owned penitentiary site for the arena itself, Jennison said. The site would then be leased to Nationwide, he added.
The arena would be one block from the Franklin County convention center, making it very attractive to the authority, Jennison said.
Columbus voters rejected a proposed 0.5 percent sales tax hike to finance a $285 million downtown arena and soccer stadium complex on May 6.
The stadium had been planned for the Columbus Crew of Major League Soccer, which has been exploring other options for staying in the metropolitan area since the vote, spokesman Adam Low said.
The Crew currently plays at the Ohio State University football stadium, which is scheduled for renovation following the 1998 season, Low said.
Crew owner Lamar Hunt has been a lead investor in the Columbus hockey expansion bid, but discussions continue about the exact ownership percentages among the group, Low said.

The NHL is considering expansion bids from Columbus, St. Paul, Atlanta, Houston, Nashville and Oklahoma City. The league has not announced how many, if any, teams it will add or decided when they would begin play.
The NHL expansion committee is scheduled to meet again Wednesday.
